# Handling of Entity Remains
The proper handling of the remains of deceased entities is necessary to maintain public health aboard the station; consequently, responsibility for collection and storage of remains falls to the Medical Department. In the event that the remains in question belong to a person, and Medical personnel have made the determination that the person cannot be reasonably restored to life through medical intervention, the following procedures should be followed:
- The person in question should be thoroughly inspected to determine cause of death, if not already known, and a determination made as to whether the person’s death was caused by foul play, misadventure, or natural causes. Findings should be transmitted to the Security and Justice Departments. - When a Nanotrasen employee expires, the Chief Medical Officer (or whosoever they may delegate the task to) should check the employee’s Medical Records to determine what wishes, if any, should be followed with regard to the disposal of their remains. - In the event that the employee has elected for burial on or around the station, Medical should contact the Chaplain and arrange for a service appropriate to the deceased final wishes. - In the event that the employee has elected to have their remains stored and transported home for burial, the remains should be stored in the morgue; if the morgue is full, Medical should ensure that sufficient decomposition-preventing body bags or other hardware are available and that all remains are properly stored within them. - The person’s remains should, at all times, be treated with respect and dignity. - Coordinate trackers should be turned off prior to interment or storage for transportation.
